correctness.rationale: For p_n=K q^n P(n), P(x)=Ax^2+Bx+C, direct geometric generating functions give a normalized positive PMF. Cancelling the geometric factor from its curvature leaves (2An+B)^2-2AP(n)-A^2, increasing strictly for n>=0 with value 4L at n=1. The survival generating function is (1-zG(z))/(1-z) for PMF generating function G. Extracting its coefficients gives the survivor at n as K q^n U(n)/(1-q), with U(n)=P(n)+(2An+B)/theta+A(theta+2)/theta^2. Clearing positive denominators in the adjacent hazard difference yields the sign of (theta/4)[P(n+1)U(n)-P(n)U(n+1)], which expands to the frozen F(n). Its quadratic and linear terms are strictly positive, so the first hazard step alone decides IFR. When H<0 there is exactly one positive real root, one change from negative to positive steps, and a flat step only if the root is integral. When H=0, the only flat step is the first. The limit is 1-q. H-L=alpha+2 alpha^2 theta>0; both are positive for alpha>=1/3 and each is a downward-opening quadratic with positive constant term for 0<alpha<1/3, giving the two stated positive roots in strict order. Both rational witnesses and their boundary signs check. This proves the infinite-index claims, independently of any finite probes.
residual_risks: This is discrete count aging for alpha,theta>0, not aging of the continuous mixing lifetime. A trough can comprise two consecutive tied ages when one hazard step is flat.

value.rationale: The two exact boundaries resolve a genuine gap in interpreting the reliability behavior of a published count family: IFR can hold without log-concavity, and the hazard can truly be nonmonotone rather than merely failing an easy sufficiency test. The whole separation band and exact turning-age rule let a reader diagnose any admissible parameters instead of relying on selected plots or isolated counterexamples.
